winner.hypothesis: Replace Caffeine write-memoization caches (createVertexCache, createEdgeCache) with ConcurrentHashMap in CachingAgeGraphOperations and CachingNeo4jGraphOperations. Caffeine's TinyLFU adds ~13-15 ns per lookup; ConcurrentHashMap is ~5 ns. createEdge does 3 lookups = saves ~25-30 ns.

all_results.notes: Compound WriteVertexEdgeKey cache collapses 3 lookups to 1. createEdge 0.041→0.014 μs (~65% improvement for that sub-score). Geomean 0.01682→0.01438 (-14.5%). Good but executor_b was better.
ConcurrentHashMap swap in CachingOps. createVertex ~0.002 μs, createEdge ~0.009 μs. All 14 sub-scores present. Winner.
BenchmarkFastMemoizingOps with plain HashMap. Only 13 sub-scores (missing age_createEdge). Disqualified from tournament due to incomplete results. createVertex 0.002 μs, neo4j_createEdge 0.007 μs.

key_findings: ConcurrentHashMap is 2-3x faster than Caffeine for small caches with no eviction pressure (~5ns vs ~13-15ns per lookup)
createVertex dropped from 0.014 to 0.002 μs (7x improvement)
createEdge dropped from 0.041 to 0.009-0.010 μs (4x improvement)
Read ops unchanged (~0.013-0.016 μs) — still using Caffeine (TTL/eviction needed)
executor_c's BenchmarkFastMemoizingOps was more aggressive (HashMap with no TTL) but had an incomplete result (missing age_createEdge)
executor_a's compound cache (3→1 lookup) also worked well (14% improvement) but ConcurrentHashMap was better
